name: Periodontal Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Periodontal Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome

criteria.description: Severe early-onset periodontitis leading to premature loss of permanent teeth
Generalized connective tissue fragility including skin hyperextensibility and easy bruising
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Absence of atrophic scarring despite skin fragility

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: severe early-onset periodontitis, connective tissue fragility, and positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for C1R or C1S mutations supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers during active periodontitis
imaging: Dental radiographs showing alveolar bone loss and root abnormalities
Echocardiography for aortic root and mitral valve assessment
other: Histopathology of gingival tissue showing connective tissue abnormalities
Clinical assessment of skin and joint hyperextensibility

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent skin fragility and hyperextensibility
Lack of systemic connective tissue features
No family history of connective tissue disorder

redFlags: Rapid progression of periodontitis with early tooth loss
Severe skin fragility with easy bruising
Family history of similar connective tissue and periodontal symptoms
references: Malfait F, et al. The 2017 international classification of the Ehlers-Danlos syndromes. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2017.
Kapferer-Seebacher I, et al. Periodontal Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is caused by mutations in C1R and C1S, which encode subcomponents C1r and C1s of complement. Am J Hum Genet. 2016.
Pepin M, et al. Clinical and genetic features of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome periodontal type. Am J Med Genet A. 2014.
